text:
Jared Spurgeon is now the most-played player in Minnesota Wild history. Reporter Heather Rule noted it after the Nov. 23 game in San Jose: "Spurgeon with an assist, +2, blocked shot, three hits in his franchise-record 1,029th game with the Wild." A sixth-round Islanders pick from 2008, he has spent his entire NHL career in Minnesota.

At 36, he's having a better year than last. He has 10 points in 18 games on 20 minutes a night, after 22 in 79 last season, and the Wild win 58.7% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him, about eight points better than without him. Some of it is luck: Minnesota has scored 8.3 more goals than expected with him on, and his 1.65 points per 60 sit well above our talent range.

The defense is still there too. Evolving-Hockey had him at 93rd percentile last season for keeping opponents' chances down, even in a down year overall, and he has 39 blocked shots already. He missed time from late October to Nov. 10, and the Wild have won six of his eight games since coming back. The record says longevity. The play says he still matters.
headline: Spurgeon's record and his bounce-back
